_about: PARKED. The grammar every move is assembled from (docs/combat/moveset-generator.md section 1). strike: a blow is a limb, a tip, a path, a target and a weight, and everything else is derived by the rules here. travel, shot and push are the parts the other stances add. What is posed is read from Animation's data (the strike and entry manifests in data/anim/waves, and data/anim/tips.json), never from this file

strike._tips: limb to tip to the paths that tip can travel. hand.heel is the bottom or the back of a closed fist; hand.plate is a blow the forearm leads; elbow.plate is both forearms as a wedge (Animation's reading of the crossed-arm ram)
strike._targets: limb to path to the places it can land. No foot reaches the head
strike._lightNever: a shape matching one of these is never light
strike._weights: The three strengths (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 2): X throws a light, Y a medium, B a heavy. A light and a medium are shapes of the grammar above. A heavy is a shape of the `heavy` block below: a whole-body blow, new
strike._animWeight: Animation's manifests still say light and heavy. Its heavy rows are today's heavy strikes, which are the mediums now. No row of Animation's is a heavy of the new tier; a posed piece that only reads on a long wind-up may stand in for one (`heavy.standIn`)
strike.legalTips: a row's tip list binds the limbs that can have those tips: a limb the row names, none of whose tips it lists, is bound whatever its tip. It was written for b03, which named elbows and knees before it named their tips; Legal's row lists every tip itself now (209272b2), so the rule is a net for the next such row
strike._links: the paths that flow out of a path: the order of a string, and of a frame's rush
strike._beat: the beat point by path, in ticks after contact (Game Design: 20 to 28)
strike._forms: the forms a move can take, by rule, and the press that asks for each (`readings` below). light: a tapped X. flurry: a mashed X. burst: a blow that fits inside the held-X burst (`burst` below). skill and juggle: X on the beat. quick: a tapped or mashed Y or B, and Y or B on the beat; a medium is quick only if it reads on a 12-tick wind-up (`windup` below). charged: a held Y or B. lift: an upward blow, for the pair X+Y and for a full charged heavy with no stick. ender and break are gone with their rules: a string no longer ends by itself, and every heavy breaks a set guard. arms is the number of arms the posed strike it starts from uses; a generated shape uses one. launch: a tap of B on a staggered rival, the launcher: a heavy that reads on half the wind-up and lands on the trunk or the head, so that it is the whole body it sends. A heavy to an arm or a leg is not a launcher: it is what the wrench is thrown with. wrench: a held B on a battered limb, with the stick on that limb: a heavy whose own place is an arm or a leg

windup._about: What a blow needs to be thrown on a wind-up shorter than it was made for. The first rule that matches is the blow's rule. `medium`: Y's 12-tick wind-up, where today's heavy strikes had 26. reads quick: thrown on a tap, in the Y flurry and on the beat, with the change given. reads charged: it only reads on a long wind-up, so it is flagged and not forced: it is thrown on a held Y only, and it may stand in for a heavy on B. `heavy`: half of B's wind-up, 14 ticks, which is the launcher on a staggered rival and, later, a heavy on the beat. reads half: it can be thrown there. reads full: it needs the whole wind-up. The ticks are Game Design's and live in Encounter's data; no tick is written here

medium.why: both feet leave together: the gather is the wind-up, and at 12 ticks it is a hop
a whole turn comes before the contact: at 12 ticks the turn is all there is to see, and in a flurry s04 bars it after any spin
both arms gather first, so no arm is left to start the flurry's next blow

medium.change: the knee lifts on the press and the leg falls from hip height: a chop of the leg, not the full swing overhead
no raise of its own: the arm starts at shoulder height, where the guard or the last blow left it, and the body drops under it
the step in is a half step: the body leans into the blow and does not travel
the hips start to turn on the press and the chamber is cut to a third: a flatter, tighter arc
no dip first: he rises from where he is. It no longer lifts by itself: the lift is the pair X+Y

windup.all: a medium does not knock back, charged or not: `sends` on a medium is only the way the reel leans

heavy.why: both feet leave together: the gather is the wind-up, and half of it is a hop
a whole turn of the whole body does not fit half the wind-up: it would land before he is round

heavy.change: the tell is cut to its last third: he is already loaded as the stagger begins, and the drive is whole

heavy._about: The third strength, on B: a whole-body blow. It is a strike shape with a drive: what the whole body does behind the limb. The path decides the drive. tips are the surfaces that can carry the weight, with the paths each travels at this weight; the places come from `targets`. No head: a headbutt is one of the vicious blows, which wait. Each drive has a tell (the wind-up as it is seen, held in plain sight for most of 28 ticks) and an end (where it leaves the body, which is where the flurry's next blow starts). flags are pose flags a drive brings to a new heavy, so that Legal's rows can judge it by machine: a whole turn is a spin

never.why: a whole-body blow to a shin is a trip, and trips belong to the clinch
the biggest rising hand to the jaw is where a leap creeps in (Legal's b03). At this weight a rising hand goes to the gut or the chest, and the jaw is an elbow's

line.what: a full pace behind the blow: the whole body travels with it and arrives as it lands
line.tell: the striking side drawn back at shoulder height, the other shoulder pointed at the rival, the weight held on the rear leg
line.end: a pace past his mark, the striking side forward
line.legal: the lead hand is open or in guard, never a pointing finger; the blow never passes through the body

arc_in.what: hips and shoulders wind away from the rival and unwind through the target: half a turn, never more
arc_in.tell: his back half turned to the rival, the striking limb carried behind the body at shoulder height
arc_in.end: turned through, the striking limb across his own centre

arc_out.what: he shows the rival his far side and the blow comes back out the way it wound: a backhand of the whole body
arc_out.tell: the striking limb crossed over his own centre, the chin over the lead shoulder
arc_out.end: opened out, the striking limb wide
arc_out.legal: one arm crosses his centre, never both forearms

rise.what: he sinks deep, and both legs drive the blow up through the target. His feet keep their place: it is not a leap
rise.tell: sunk under the rival's guard with the striking limb loaded below the target, the back straight
rise.end: stood up to his full height, the striking limb high
rise.legal: a lunge-low stance, the other hand up in guard; never both fists clenched at the sides in a crouch; no scream, no aura, no ground cracking; no leap. Legal has seen one drawn in Animation's study and passed it (RL-106)

drop.what: he rises over the target and comes down on it with his whole weight
drop.tell: risen above the rival with the striking limb carried at shoulder height; it lifts only as he starts down
drop.end: sunk below where he began, the striking limb low
drop.legal: the rise is the body straightening or stepping up, never a leap; the limb at shoulder height until he starts down; one arm. Legal has seen one drawn in Animation's study and passed it (RL-106)

spin.what: one whole turn in place, wound up in plain sight; never two, never travelling
spin.tell: the shoulders turned away and the head already looking back over them
spin.end: facing the rival again, a quarter turn past
spin.legal: one turn, in place, never travelling

heavy._words: a heavy's plain name is its drive's word, its tip's word and its place: a stepping fist to the chest, a falling heel to the chest. Animation reads these
heavy.standIn: a posed medium whose wind-up rule reads charged covers the heavy of the same shape at the level stand_in: it can play on B at 28 ticks today, as a derived move, until the tier's own poses exist

launcher._about: The launcher (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 3): a tap of B on a staggered rival always lands and launches. Which heavy is thrown is picked by where it sends, from the stick's lean. The stick nudges and the director stages the launch itself; this is only the blow that starts it
launcher._aim: the stick's lean to the send wanted: up lifts him, down drives him under, toward drives him back along the line, away turns him past the attacker. Each direction owns 45 degrees either side, and a diagonal reads as up or down (Game Design, section 3 of the design page)
launcher._noStick: with no stick the launch planner picks where he goes, and the blow is a launcher that sends that way: never just any
launcher._wrench: the wrench: a charged heavy on a battered limb is the crippling blow. The stick picks the limb by the same map (away the arms, down the legs), and the piece has to land there: it is a heavy whose own place is that limb (the form wrench). A wrench never launches; a tapped heavy and the launcher never wrench

burst._about: The burst: a held X throws eight lights that slow on a curve (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 3). The first is the light the press threw. Each later blow is drawn from the X cell by the class of the gap before it, under the string rules and the rules below, which are what keep a 4-tick gap from reading as a stutter. The gaps are Game Design's and live in Encounter's data: the classes name them, and no tick is written on a move

open.why: whatever light the tap would have thrown

fast.why: only a hand gets out and back inside 5 ticks, and only on a path with no raise and no turn. The hands alternate, which Animation's speed look already does

mid.why: an elbow or a knee fits once the gap opens

slow.why: any light: the last two may be kicks or dropping blows, and the eighth is the close when nothing has answered

noStutter.rule: never the same limb, tip and path twice running: the same blow thrown again 4 ticks later is a stutter
never the same place twice running: the sparks would stack on one point
no more than two blows running on one path: three straights read as one blow played three times
no piece twice in one burst

strike._swap: hand tips a key set can show by a hand-state swap, where the tip can travel that path (Animation: confirmed; a beat's own tip wins)
strike._tagTips: a key set that carries one of Legal's tags keeps to these tips when its hand state is swapped
strike._reaim: how far a key set's contact can be re-aimed is Animation's measured table, one row a key set: ok is free, edge lands but strains and needs a look

banned.why: two hands with wrists together pushed forward: a famous beam-release pose
hands cupped at a hip, or drawn back to one hip and thrust: the franchise's best-known wind-up. Applies to every weight and every form, including held heavies
banned.appliesTo: open or clawed hands (a closed fist chambered at the hip is a punch chamber and passes b02; h05 still holds a 12-tick wind-up to the shoulder)

banned.why: a rising blow with a leap or a spin, by hand, elbow or knee: the jumping, turning uppercut
banned.appliesTo: any tip of a hand, elbow or knee on a rise path to the jaw or head: a rising blow bound by this row whatever its tip (Combat's strict reading)

banned.why: more than a single turn, or a spin that travels: a multi-hit whirling kick
two clasped fists brought down: the double axe-handle smash
a clawed hand or grip on the face
grips on the throat, hair or tail are never used (the grab rules)
an arm passing through the body
a melee piece never carries light, a ball or a raised charging pose
two fingers or a pointing finger, or a hand to the forehead: the franchise's beam and teleport poses
a held or charged medium or heavy is loaded with one arm drawn back at shoulder height, never at a hip and never with both hands together; the new words medium and charged loosen nothing
no vanish or blink between blows; the fighter is drawn the whole way

strike._banned: Legal's shape rows (docs/legal/movegen-banned.json, RL-073), merged as they stand. A row matches when every field it names matches; a list matches on any of its values; form matches any of a move's forms; flags matches any flag the move is known to have. The generator never emits a match, and --check fails on one. Rows are only added, never removed, without Legal

bannedSequences.rule: no more than 3 pieces in a row with the same limb, tip and path
bannedSequences.why: a barrage of identical blows is a famous shouted-barrage signature

bannedSequences.rule: no more than 2 blows in a row to the same target, and never two to the gut in a row
bannedSequences.why: a stomach-punch trade; also keeps Blow for Blow ours

bannedSequences.rule: a flurry never repeats a shouted syllable across its blows
bannedSequences.why: a chanted barrage; audio and the generator both enforce it

bannedSequences.rule: a spin is never followed by another spin, and never by a head kick
bannedSequences.why: a multi-turn whirl; also the grammar's light rule

bannedSequences.rule: a rising blow is never followed by another rising blow while he is airborne
a launch is never followed by a clasped two-hand overhead blow
no string places a piece after a step that is not drawn: no vanish, blink or teleport step

inside a hold, vicious blows run no more than 2 in a row to the same place, and the arm counts as three places (shoulder, elbow, wrist) and the head, core and legs as two each, so four taps on one region alternate places; vicious blows are strikes, never a grip on the throat, hair or tail, and never a clawed hand on the face; the sound rule f03 holds across the taps
bannedSequences.why: s02 applied to the clinch; Orb's design and the rating question are still open (not cleared by this row)

strike._bannedSequences: Legal's sequence rules, each with a form a program can check beside Legal's words. run: at most `max` blows in a row that share the parts in `same` (tighter: a smaller max where a filter holds). after: a blow matching `after` is never followed by one matching a `never` filter (state: only in that state at run time; the generator's own strings obey it always). steps: a string uses only drawn steps. audio: not checkable from parts; Audio and the director's line picker hold it

flags._about: How a move gets the pose flags Legal's rows name. A flag is known present, known absent, or unknown. Known present: the generator's own rules below, or a `flags` list on the manifest row of the key set it starts from (Animation's data; no row has one yet). Known absent: the key set carries the Legal tag that rules the flag out (`clearedBy`). Unknown otherwise: the row then becomes an ask in the sheet's Legal column, not a refusal
flags.fromTip: identity.json `tipFlags`: a fighter's way of showing a tip (the rival's palm is drawn clawed)
flags._byVocabulary: flags no part of the grammar can produce: there is no such hand state, target or step. A new one is new vocabulary and gets Legal's screen

conditions.ask: a rising blow, by hand, elbow or knee: feet stay down, no turn, the limb lowers at once, no glow; never strung into another rising blow in the air
a palm strike: a blow only, nothing leaves the hand; never chambered at a hip; never a clawed hand on the face
a dropping blow: one fist, blade or plate; two hands stay apart; never clasped, never held raised
a straight blow to the gut or chest: it never passes through the body; strung, never a run at one place
a spin: a single turn, never travelling; never followed by another spin
held: a charged medium or heavy is charged with one arm drawn back at shoulder height; never at a hip, never both hands together, no light
a crossed-arm ram: the arms cross only for the strike, wrists apart, never a held cross
to the head or jaw: a strike, never a grip

a zip: the body is drawn and opaque on every tick of the way in and out, each at least 4 ticks; echoes trail behind it and never stand where he will arrive; a far-side exit goes over the rival or round him after the blow
a grab: it holds the collar, shoulder, upper arm, body, waist or ankle, never the throat, hair, tail or face; no locked or laced hands, nothing lit at the hands; a carry is drawn whole

an energy hand: one hand, open or a blade, no higher than the shoulder; the light sits on the plate or the hand's edge, never a ball at the hand; never two fingers or a point, never cupped, never both hands; a beam or charged shot is a straight line; a volley is one sweep, flick or single thrust of one hand, never pumped
a push: a shove on the chest or gut, no light, hands apart when it is two; never a grip
stacking: at every tick of a tell or a charge, no more than two of the seven power-up marks; a stance's aura is a thin outline or short streaks in the lane colour

a held pose: held 12 ticks or more, it is judged by its class (legal.heldScope): the pair test on every held pose, the emitter test on charges, tells, signatures, energy poses and a held heavy's hold; no held crossed forearms and no arms-wide invitation (a shrug is not one); a signature's tell is its own stance, never a crouch with clenched fists, and has no scream

a wind-up of 12 ticks or more, which is every medium and every heavy: a held pose, judged at every tick: the loaded limb at shoulder height or lower (a leg may be chambered), never at a hip for any hand state, never both hands together, no limb above 80 except in the last 6 ticks before contact, no held crossed forearms, no light and no aura; a both-hand blow keeps its hands at least shoulder width apart

the burst: it never repeats the last blow's limb, tip and path, or its place; no more than two blows running on one path; no piece twice; the hands alternate; at any instant at most 2 ghosts of any limb and 4 limb-ghosts in all; a gap under 6 ticks runs for 3 blows at most, in its opening only; one breath of sound for the eight; no slow-motion close-up or camera cut on it. Its opening three blows are seen drawn first

conditions.from: Legal's screen of the three strengths
conditions.ask: a stepping heavy: the lead hand is open or in guard, never a pointing finger; the blow never passes through the body

conditions.from: Legal's screen of the three strengths
conditions.ask: a turning heavy: half a turn, never more

conditions.from: Legal's screen of the three strengths
conditions.ask: an unwinding heavy: one arm crosses his centre, never both forearms

conditions.from: Legal's screen of the three strengths
conditions.ask: a heaving heavy: a lunge-low stance with the striking limb loaded and the other hand up in guard; never both fists clenched at the sides in a crouch; no scream, no aura, no ground cracking; the feet keep their place

conditions.from: Legal's screen of the three strengths
conditions.ask: a falling heavy: the rise is the body straightening or stepping up, never a leap; the limb stays at shoulder height until he starts down; one arm only, never both palms or both fists

conditions.from: Legal's screen of the three strengths
conditions.ask: a stand-in on B's 28 ticks: a held pose, judged on the longer wind-up. A double hammer or a double palm keeps its hands at least shoulder width apart and at or below shoulder height, with a raise overhead only in the last 6 ticks, or it is dropped as a stand-in. A crossed-arm ram crosses only for the strike. A spin is a single turn in place. A drop kick's gather is not a crouch with fists clenched at the sides

conditions.from: Legal's e08 (Combat's R1, adopted) and e09
conditions.ask: an energy blow in reach: one open, blade or lit-fist hand at shoulder height or lower; the hand is lit as a thin edge before it lands, never a ball; a blade hand is a flat blade, never a pointed finger or two fingers; a lit fist's light sits on its plate and knuckle edges only; the shot goes off at the contact as a thin edge or a short cone; each body takes a rim of its colour on the near side, never a flash over the whole body; never at the face; mashed, the piece changes every blow (hand state, release) and at most one blow in 20 ticks gets the full flash, counted over the whole screen; the blast's 12-tick wind-up is a held pose, its gather a thin ring or edge at the palm. A mashed run reads as varied on screen (e09): never the same arm, path and place twice running; no regular left-right pump, the free arm taking a bolt now and then; three different paths in any five; each hand below the collar line on the chest or the gut; a hand's width between the heads. The contact, the cone, the rim and a mashed run are seen drawn first

strike._conditions: Legal's conditions from its screen of the sheet (docs/legal/movegen-screen.md section 1), for Animation: the sheet's Legal column lists the ids that apply to a row. They bite when a move is held or strung

travel._about: The manoeuvre stance: how he gets to the blow. A move is a kind, a direction, the entry that carries him, the way out, and a blow from one of his strike cells whose path suits the direction

zip.what: in, the blow, and out again (docs/design/melee-press-feel.md section 2c)

zip_away.what: leaving a brawl with a parting blow

step.what: a step of up to 2 bh around, over or under the rival, and the blow

pursuit.what: the pursuit past charge range, into a heavy

travel._arrive: direction to the paths a blow can land on from there: a rise from under, a drop from over, an arc from around

shot._about: The energy arts stance: the shot's kind is the cell's, and a move is how it is thrown. hand comes from the fighter's own list (identity.json energy.hands)

rules.why: a lob is one shot, thrown from a footing
three bolts in a tight fan leave on a flick or a thrust

hands._about: Every energy hand, for both fighters: its shape, where its light sits, how many hands and how high. A hand not listed here is new vocabulary and needs Legal's screen

pinch._note: thumb to forefinger, never two fingers

fist_glow._note: the lit fist: light on the plate and the knuckle edges, never a sphere round the fist

reach._about: Energy in reach (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 5b): with RB held in a brawl, X is the point-blank bolt and Y the blast. A piece is an energy hand of the fighter's own, how it is let go, and the place it is set on: a blow and a shot at once. It takes a light's or a medium's place in a string, so it has a path (by its release) and a place, and Legal's string rules count it with the blows. No piece is aimed at the head. The body is the brawl's own, leaned by the stick
reach._path: thrust: the hand is driven in and the shot leaves along the arm. flick: the back of the hand snaps out and the shot leaves off it. sweep: the hand is drawn across him and the shot leaves along the sweep

rules.why: the blast is braced and let go on a straight line

run._about: A mashed run of point-blank bolts, ordered by Legal's e09 so that it reads as varied on screen and not only in data. An arm is lead or free: which arm throws a bolt is chosen for each throw, and Animation mirrors the piece. samePlacePathArm: never the same arm, path and place twice running. pathsIn: at least so many different paths in any so many bolts running. freeArm: the free arm takes a bolt now and then, never two in three (so never a left-right pump), at least one in six, and never on a regular count (two gaps running between its bolts are never equal). notPeriodic: the order of the pieces never repeats on a fixed count of 3 or 4. A run also keeps what every string keeps: never one of his last two pieces, e06, and the string rules. Each hand lands on the chest or the gut, below the collar line; the heads keep a hand's width apart (Animation)
run._proof: a run of this many bolts must exist for each fighter (three seconds of mashing, the length Legal will watch): --check tries to make one

readings._about: Which form each press of a strike button asks for (docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md section 8). One press is one attack: a button's pool is one list, and the press picks the form. The held X is not a form: it is a string of eight from the same pool (`strike.burst`, and the cell's `presses.hold`)

legal._about: Legal's row groups beyond the strike rows (docs/legal/movegen-banned.json, RL-076 and RL-081 to RL-086), merged as they stand: every row keeps Legal's rule and why. Where the parts allow it a row gains a form a program can check (kind travel, hand, move or holdPoints), and the generator refuses a match; the rest are about how a thing is drawn, lit or timed, and are conditions for their owner. --check fails if a row here differs from Legal's file

applies.strike.banned: strike pieces only: the martial cells, the checks, the pushes, and the blow of a zip, a step or a charge. An energy piece is judged by the energy rows: b09 would refuse a lit fist, and e01 is the rule for where an energy hand's light may sit

motion.rule: a zip (any reading) is drawn on every tick: the body is visible and opaque on each tick of the way in and the way out, never hidden, faded or swapped for a copy

motion.check: a zip's way in and way out are each at least max(4, ceil(bh / 3)) ticks
motion.rule: a zip's way in and its way out each last at least 4 ticks, and consecutive drawn positions are at most 3 body heights apart (ticks >= max(4, ceil(distance in bh / 3)))
motion.why: a zero or two-tick jump with echoes is a blink step

motion.rule: the path is continuous: the body passes through every point between start and arrival, and any copy or echo trails behind the body, never ahead of it, never at the arrival point before the body gets there
motion.why: an afterimage that stands where he is about to appear is the vanish-step staging

motion.rule: a far-side exit is its own drawn travel that starts after the strike hold, over the rival or round him, with the rival's body in view throughout; he never appears behind the rival in the same tick as the strike
motion.why: the appear-behind-you beat needs the vanish

motion.rule: a zip ghost is a flat single tint in the fighter's lane colour (never the body's own colours or face), opacity 0.35 or less and fainter for older ones, at most 5 per zip, on the body's real recent path, each overlapping the next by about a third so they read as a smear, never in a ring, fan or spread round the target, gone within 8 ticks of the zip's end
motion.why: filled ghosts are allowed as a blur, not as a lineup of body copies

motion.rule: the body is always drawn on top of its ghosts at full opacity, and no ghost stays behind as a stationary copy
motion.why: a decoy copy is a separate signature

motion.rule: a heavy's wind-up ring is hollow, thin, in the lane colour, shrinks onto the striking fist and never grows or holds, lasts the wind-up only (10 ticks or fewer), and never fills or becomes a ball at the hand
motion.why: a charging-pose cue under the stacking rule

motion.rule: outcome marks (counter bar, closing ring, brackets, guard fragments) carry no text or numbers, never sit on the eyes or face, and are never a full-screen or body-wide gold, white or red flash
motion.why: no readout or scanner look, no mark 7

motion.rule: in a zip chain each hop meets m01 to m08 on its own: the strike pose is held at least 4 ticks at contact with the body drawn, the ghosts on screen across the whole chain are at most 5, no ghost is left behind or placed round the target, and there is no camera cut or flash between hops
a zip at a launched rival follows his drawn body along a continuous path; it never snaps to where he will land

motion.check: a slip or a step behind the rival is drawn travel of at least 4 ticks
motion.rule: a slip or a step that goes behind the rival is drawn travel of at least 4 ticks with the rival in view (m04)

energy.rule: no sphere or ball in or at the hand, at rest or growing; a charge is light on the forearm plate or hand edge, and the blast leaves along a line
an energy hand is open or a blade, no higher than the shoulder; never cupped, never both hands pushed from the chest or drawn to a hip, never wrists together (b01, b02)
no two extended fingers, no single pointing finger as an emitter; the pinch is thumb to forefinger only (b10)
energy.why: the beam and the death-beam poses

energy.rule: a short beam or charged shot is a plain straight line: no spiral, drilling or twisting beam; a second hand may brace the arm but never grips the firing wrist and never sits cupped under it

a volley is one motion of one hand or arm (a sweep, a flick or a single thrust) that releases the fan; never both palms pumping forward in turn or one hand pumping repeatedly, and no repeated shouted syllable across it (s03)

a burst, a blast and a ki-style flurry (B), and an energy blow in reach (RB + X or Y), are thrown by one hand at shoulder height or lower: an open hand, a blade hand, or the rival's lit fist with the light on its plate and knuckle edges only (the cleared fist glow), never a ball or glow round the fist; a flurry varies the piece (hand state, release, body) and never pumps the same hand repeatedly or both palms in turn; a point-blank blast shows its flash as a thin edge or short cone at the hand, never a ball; never aimed at the face
energy.why: the shouted two-palm barrage and the held sphere; the lit fist was cleared in RL-062 and is not banned by e02 or e06

energy.rule: a beam held and steered by the player stays a plain straight line; steering moves the aim or the origin only, never twists, spirals or whips the beam, and the firing pose does not change while it is held

R1 adopted: an energy blow in reach is one open, blade or lit-fist hand at shoulder height or lower, lit as a thin edge before it lands, the shot going off at contact as a thin edge or short cone, each body taking a rim of its colour on the near side and never a flash over the whole body; never at the face; mashed, the piece changes every blow (hand state, release) and at most one blow in 20 ticks gets the full flash; the blast's 12-tick wind-up is a held pose (h05) with its gather a thin ring or edge at the palm; the blade hand is a flat blade, never a pointed finger or two fingers (e03)
energy.why: R1 with the lit fist and the finger rule added

energy.rule: a mashed run of point-blank bolts must read as varied on screen, not only in data: no two bolts in a row with the same arm, path and place; no regular left-right alternation (an irregular order, with the free arm taking a bolt now and then); at least three different paths (line, outward arc, inward arc) in any five; each hand lands below the collar line on the chest or gut and never at the neck, throat or face; the two bodies keep a hand's width between the heads
energy.why: e06 for a mashed run: the same arm pumping, or two palms pumping in turn, is the barrage image

grabs.rule: a hold point is the collar, shoulder, upper arm, body, waist or ankle; never the throat, the hair or a tail (b07), never a clawed hand on the face (b06)
no hands locked or laced between the two fighters at any time, and nothing glowing at the hands in a hold
a lift or carry is drawn whole: the carried fighter's body is in view and never hidden by a zip or a cut; a throw is a launch (the planner), not a vanish

a tackle takes the body at the waist or shoulders; the carry is drawn travel (m01 to m04 apply: at least 4 ticks, the carried body in view every tick, 3 bh a tick at most); the arrival crater is local, with debris falling and no rising ring of rubble, no lightning and no aura; a buried rival is shown partly in the ground, never hidden

a clinch is a collar-and-elbow or waist hold; the trip and the throw never lift by the throat, hair or a tail, and the two fighters' hands are never locked or laced together; no sparks or glow at the hands in the clinch
grabs.why: g01 and g02 applied to the clinch

held.owner: Animation (a lint on poses held 12 ticks or more)
held.rule: held 12 ticks or more, scoped by class (see heldScope): the pair test applies to every held pose; the emitter test applies to the charge, tell, signature, energy and hold classes only

held.owner: Animation (a lint on poses held 12 ticks or more)
held.rule: no held crossed forearms; no held arms-wide invitation. Arms wide means both arms near straight (elbows within 25 degrees of straight) and both hands 32 or more out to opposite sides, held 12 ticks or more; a shrug (elbows bent 40 degrees or more, palms up, shoulders raised) is not arms wide. A taker's open-armed stance belongs to the rival's On the Chin alone
held.why: the power pose and the take-it stance

held.owner: Animation (a lint on poses held 12 ticks or more)
held.rule: a signature's tell is its own stance, never a crouch with fists clenched at the sides, and carries no scream

held.owner: Animation (a lint on poses held 12 ticks or more)
held.rule: held-lint classes for the new holds: a held X, Y or B charge pose and the tackle's coil are class charge; the seize, breaker, lift and slip tells are class tell; the clinch hold is class hold; the 45-tick taunt is class gesture; an open-hand chamber in a charged melee blow keeps the wrist at x 9 or more (not drawn to the hip), a closed-fist chamber at the hip is allowed
held.why: so the lint reaches the new poses

held.rule: a medium or heavy wind-up of 12 ticks or more is a held pose of class charge and is judged at every tick by h01 to h04: the loaded limb at shoulder height or lower (a leg may be chambered), never at a hip for any hand state, never both hands together, no limb held above 80 except in the last 6 ticks before contact, no held crossed forearms, no light and no aura; both-hand blows (a double palm or hammer) keep the hands at least shoulder width apart; a stand-in played on a longer wind-up than it was posed for is judged on the longer one (W1)
held.why: W1 adopted; a long visible wind-up is a held pose

held.owner: Animation (a lint on poses held 12 ticks or more)
held.rule: a deep sink (the heaving drive) is a lunge-low stance with the striking limb loaded and the other hand up in guard; never both fists clenched at the sides in a crouch, and never with a scream, an aura or ground cracking; the falling drive's rise is the body straightening or stepping up, never a leap (the drop kick excepted, as cleared), and the limb stays at shoulder height until he starts down
held.why: mark 1 over a held sink; the leap and the held raise

held.owner: Animation (a lint on poses held 12 ticks or more)
held.rule: a manner (the rival's show-off, the Protagonist's pointed) is a way of throwing, not a gesture: the rival's open tell keeps the limb drawn back (never arms spread as an invitation, never a beckon), and his limb left out after landing lasts 12 ticks or fewer; no taunt pose is part of a blow

stacking.rule: at any tick, no more than two of the seven marks (crouch with clenched fists, scream, upward flame aura, rubble ring with ground crack and wind, lightning on the body, hair change, a flash with a shouted form name); a held tell or a 45-tick charge is checked at every tick, not once
a stance tell's aura is a thin outline or short scattered streaks in the lane colour; a manoeuvre trail is thin and in the lane colour; a defensive rim of light sits on the guarding side only

a charge flash or ring (a tier mark at 16 or 24 ticks for a medium, 32 or 44 for a heavy, a full-charge flash, or the wind-up ring) is a thin ring or edge flash on the charging hand, forearm or plate, in the lane colour, 4 ticks or fewer, never body-wide, never gold, white or red, never with a shouted name; a wind-up ring is hollow, thin, lane-coloured and shrinks onto the limb (m07); a held charge shows at most two of the seven marks at any tick, and no scream at any tier. Tick counts are the design's and may change: the conditions, not the numbers, are the rule
stacking.why: marks 3, 7 and 2 across a held charge; restated to the three-strength spec

stacking.rule: a mutual throw-back, a spark-lock between two heavy commitments, a power-attack tell and a taunt's finish show no rubble ring with cracks and wind, no lightning on bodies, no body-wide aura and no gold, white or red flash; sparks sit at the contact point only

full flashes are counted over the whole screen, every effect and both fighters together: at most three in any one second, each small (a thin edge or short cone), none red, and a reduced-motion setting halves the rate; the cap is checked by a flash analysis of a recorded mashed sequence on the real build
stacking.why: photosensitivity; Combat's one in 20 ticks is the same 3 a second

flurry.rule: a flurry's or burst's blur follows each striking limb's real path: at any instant at most 2 ghosts of any limb and at most 4 limb-ghosts on screen in all; never extra arms, legs or fists drawn at once, never a fan of limbs round the target. This replaces the 'two ghosts per blow' wording, which does not hold at 15 blows a second. The numbers are ceilings on what is alive at one instant, not counts that must be drawn: fewer is always fine, reduced motion draws fewer, and a tech blow's 3 wire echoes that pop off in turn with never more than 2 alive at once meet it. Body ghosts of a zip fall under m05 (at most 5)
flurry.why: the many-armed barrage blur, by instant rather than by blow

flurry.rule: targets and pieces rotate across the whole string, whatever mix of X, Y and B made it: s01 and s02 count the string, not the button (no more than 2 blows in a row to the same target, never two gut blows running, no more than 3 of the same limb, tip and path)
flurry.why: a mixed flurry must not slip past the repeat rules by changing button

flurry.rule: vocal sounds in a flurry: no repeated shouted syllable across it, no shouted word, and at most one grunt for every two blows, varied
flurry.why: the chanted barrage (s03) at up to 10 blows a second

flurry.rule: a gap of under 6 ticks between blows never runs for more than 3 blows in a row, and only inside the opening of a burst; blows then slow (a held X's 4, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, 15 gaps are within this)
flurry.why: the fastest barrage rate is allowed only as a short opening, not a sustained storm

flurry.rule: a burst (held X, eight lights) never repeats the last blow's limb, tip, path or place; no more than 2 blows in a row on one path; no piece twice in one burst; the hands alternate; the sound is one breath for the eight, never a syllable for each; no slow-motion close-up or camera cut on the burst

heldScope._about: Legal's scope for the held-pose lint (2026-10-06). A pose's class comes from its sequence family, or from a `_legal.class` mark on the pose or sequence. Unmarked poses in the charging, tell, signature, energy and held-heavy families are lint class charge, tell, signature, energy or hold; every other unmarked pose is rest or gesture.

energy: emitter holds, beams, channel, release, rain, finish holds

pairTest.fails: both hands within 10 units of each other AND both in the hip zone (x 14 or less, height 24 to 44); or both wrists forward and within 7 units of each other (wrists_together)
pairTest.exempt: a named gesture where one hand holds or brushes the other hand or wrist (the cuff, the dusting, the close taunt tap) with the body upright and no thrust or light after it

emitterTest.applies: classes charge, tell, signature, energy, hold
emitterTest.fails: the hand that emits or strikes next is an open or clawed hand in the hip zone with its wrist at x 8 or less (drawn to a hip then thrust); or any hand above 82 (80 plus a 2-unit tolerance for float error). A closed fist chambered at the hip (a punch chamber) and a relaxed free hand hanging at the side while the other arm acts both pass

armsWideTest.applies: class charge, tell, signature, energy, hold, and any held pose that is not marked gesture with bent elbows
armsWideTest.fails: both arms near straight and out wide, held 12 ticks or more, except the rival's On the Chin

grab._about: Where a grab may take hold (Legal g01, g04, g05). No grab is generated yet: the context cells list today's

vicious._about: PLAN, for slice C4b: inside the clinch each further tap of A is a vicious blow on the region the stick leans to, up to four. Nothing is generated from this block yet. regions: the stick's lean to the region (Game Design, 68b9a586); with no stick, the core. places: the places a region has, for Legal's s08: no more than two blows running to one place, so four taps on a region alternate. An arm is three places. A vicious blow is a strike, never a grip
